recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR core follow-up is needed unless Pharmacy reopens the broader question of how to represent non-user-selected source/definitive medication codes.
issue_request: FHIR-12391 asked whether Medication.code needed a separate definitive/source Coding distinct from descriptive translations. The Published Pharmacy resolution was Not Persuasive with Modification: do not add a new element, but update the Medication.code comment to say the user-selected code has coding.userSelected=true and to reference Coding datatype guidance.
initial_application: The issue was historically applied by git-svn commit 6ef7a79e5d50d39ae6d127dc66cada986d958001, which named TR#12391 and updated the then-authoritative Medication spreadsheet source. The wording was later carried into source/medication/structuredefinition-Medication.xml after the current source refactor.
additional_context: Medication is active/approved in source/fhir.ini, so source/medication/structuredefinition-Medication.xml is current build source. The Coding datatype narrative still supplies the referenced userSelected semantics. Later same-element work for FHIR-45876 changed Medication.code short/definition text for code.text medication names, left the FHIR-12391 comment intact, and is already represented on the combined branch. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no FHIR-12391-specific discussion or conflicting later Pharmacy decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source edit was made because Medication.code already tells implementers that the code selected by the user has coding.userSelected=true and preserves translation/granularity guidance; adding a separate definitive Coding element would contradict the issue's final disposition.
